content: Yotta describes Shakti Cloud as a sovereign AI cloud and GPU computing platform for AI work in India.
Yotta's AI Lab description mentions NVIDIA H100 and L40S for managed notebooks.
Neysa presents Velocis as an AI acceleration cloud for building, deploying and scaling AI.
Together AI's cloud overview identifies B200, GB200, GB300, H100 and H200 hardware.
Together AI publishes separate pricing sections for serverless inference and provisioned throughput.
RunPod addresses AI developers and presents Pods, Serverless, Clusters and Hub as different ways to build and deploy workloads.
RunPod's GPU Cloud Pricing page mentions A100, B200, H100, H200, L40S and RTX 4090.
RunPod publishes separate pricing categories for Pods, Serverless, Clusters and Reserved Clusters.
RunPod describes dedicated Serverless GPU API endpoints with bring-your-container deployment and network storage.
Lambda positions its cloud offering around supercomputers for training and inference.
Nebius presents a cloud spanning AI training and inference, and emphasizes repeatable self-service cluster setup.
The Nebius cloud overview mentions NVIDIA H100 hardware.
CoreWeave positions its cloud platform as purpose-built for demanding AI workloads.
Crusoe Cloud lists NVIDIA GB200, B200, H200 and H100 among its GPU options.
Crusoe Cloud highlights building, training and serving models within one cloud.
VAST Data positions its platform as AI-era data infrastructure and invites prospects to a weekly live demo.
Voltage Park positions its service as foundational AI infrastructure for demanding workloads.
Voltage Park's site highlights NVIDIA HGX H100 GPUs.
Hyperstack's pricing page references A100, B200, GB200, GB300, H100, H200 and L40 GPU options.
Hyperstack distinguishes on-demand, reserved and spot GPU VM pricing.
The Foundry domain presents Mithril as an AI compute platform for businesses and research organizations.
